title: Nineteen Eighty-Four
author: George Orwell
premise: A totalitarian regime known as the Party, led by the omnipresent Big Brother, exercises complete control over the public through constant surveillance, historical negationism, and propaganda.

major_characters.name: Winston Smith
major_characters.occupation: Clerk at the Ministry of Truth (Records Department)
major_characters.description: A middle-aged Party member who secretly harbors resentment toward the regime and seeks rebellion.

major_characters.name: Julia
major_characters.occupation: Worker in the Fiction Department at the Ministry of Truth
major_characters.description: A pragmatic rebel who opposes the Party through personal, covert acts of defiance.

major_characters.name: O'Brien
major_characters.description: A powerful and manipulative agent of the Thought Police who poses as a dissident to entrap Winston.

major_characters.name: Big Brother
major_characters.description: The enigmatic leader of Oceania and the face of the Party's supreme authority.

major_characters.name: Emmanuel Goldstein
major_characters.description: The alleged leader of the underground resistance known as the Brotherhood.

ministries.name: Ministry of Truth (Minitrue)
ministries.function: Propaganda, historical revisionism, and media control

ministries.name: Ministry of Love (Miniluv)
ministries.function: Law enforcement, political interrogation, torture, and thought control

ministries.name: Ministry of Plenty (Miniplenty)
ministries.function: Rationing, economic control, and manufactured scarcity

key_concepts.definition: The psychological ability to hold two contradictory beliefs simultaneously and accept both as true.
The official language of Oceania designed to limit freedom of thought by eliminating words capable of expressing dissent.
Holding opinions, thoughts, or beliefs unapproved by the Party.
A two-way television device used for broadcasting propaganda and conducting continuous surveillance.
A daily ritual where Party members vent collective rage against Goldstein and foreign enemies.
The torture chamber in the Ministry of Love that subjects prisoners to their worst individual fears.

themes: The power of language over independent thought
Historical revisionism and the destruction of truth
